properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 4 at 10:56PM CDT until October 5 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 4 at 10:55PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
At 1054 PM CDT...A line of strong thunderstorms was located along a
line extending from 18 nm west of Oriskany Reef to 55 nm south of
Farewell Buoy...moving east at 20 knots.

These storms will remain over mainly open waters.

The primary threats from these storms are wind gusts up to 30
knots...locally higher waves...and heavy downpours. Boaters should
consider seeking safe harbor until these storms have passed.

Weather conditions support the development of waterspouts.
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
waves and seas. If a waterspout is sighted...seek safe harbor
immediately.

To report severe weather...call (800) 284-9059.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Copper Valley; Western Copper Valley; Central Copper Valley; Ernestine; Southern Copper Valley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 7:50PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Areas of locally dense fog will persist along portions of the
Glenn and Richardson Highways, especially from Glennallen west to
Mendeltna, this evening through early Monday morning.

Periods of a wintry mix of precipitation are also expected across
the Copper River Basin through Monday morning. With temperatures
around freezing for most locations, any precipitation may fall as
a mix of rain, snow, and freezing drizzle. Little to no
significant snow and ice accumulation is expected. However, the
combination of falling precipitation and temperatures around
freezing may result in slippery road conditions and patchy black
ice. The precipitation and fog is expected to taper off by early
to mid Monday morning.

Motorists are urged to slow down and use caution while traveling.
For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit
511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: AREAS OF DENSE FOG ALONG WITH PERIODS OF A WINTRY MIX OF RAIN, SNOW, AND FREEZING DRIZZLE FOR THE CENTRAL COPPER RIVER BASIN THROUGH MONDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 4 at 11:49PM EDT until October 5 at 1:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
FFWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Charleston County in southeastern South Carolina...

* Until 100 AM EDT.

* At 1149 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, Isle Of Palms, Awendaw, Price Inlet, Capers Inlet,
Bull Island, Capers Island, Dewees Island and Whitehall Terrace.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Capers Island, Bulls Bay, Wando River, Dewees Island, US-17
Charleston National, Mt Pleasant Airport and Bull Island.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

markers 205 and 235. US Highway 231 between mile markers 78 and 88.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 4 at 7:33PM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves are expected
due to elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet. Abnormally high morning and
evening tides of 6.5 to 7 ft are expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Most
susceptible areas will be Long Beach and Avalon Harbor Tuesday
and Wednesday. Then, Malibu to Ventura Wednesday through
Friday.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
morning and evening high tides, including over beach parking
lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion
is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a moderate chance that an
upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory and/or High Surf Advisory
will be needed. These products will likely need to be extended
into the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
